the aryl hydrocarbon (AhR) receptor regulates the focal adhesion kinase/Src (FAK/Src) pathway and promotes the migration of breast epithelial cells.

the regulation of cell adhesion and motility by the AhR and the potential contribution of the AhR to the metastatic process.
the non-genomic effects of ligand binding to the AhR, specifically the activation of Src and FAK.
the non-genomic effects of xenobiotics on the regulation of cell adhesion and migration.

the AhR regulates focal adhesions through a non-genomics Src/FAK pathway, and this pathway contributes to cell migration.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AhR ligands activate Src, which in turn activates FAK.
AhR ligands, such as 2,3,7,8-tetrachlorodibenzo-p-dioxin (TCDD), can promote cell migration through non-genomic pathways, such as the FAK/Src/HEF1/NED9 axis.

the AhR is a non-genomic signaling receptor, which regulates the activation of FAK and Src.
the AhR regulates focal adhesion signaling through a Src-dependent pathway.
the AhR is not only a xenobiotic sensor, but also a regulator of cell migration.
